description.markdown:
The Citizens' Police Complaint Board (CPCB) reviews complaints brought to the attention of the Citizens’ Police Complaint Office (CPCO).

The board is made up of 9 voting members from the community and 3 non-voting police officers, for a total of 12 members. The Mayor appoints three members and one IMPD member, the City-County Council appoints six members and one IMPD member, and the Fraternal Order of Police appoints one member.

The board generally meets on the second Monday of each month at 6:00 p.m., but no less than quarterly, to conduct business.

Non-IMPD members are appointed to three-year terms and must complete 20 hours of training in police procedures and 16 hours of ride-alongs with an IMPD officer per year.

[Click to view the list of current board members.](https://indianapolis.granicus.com/boards/w/f4a1ea9c05a8da69/boards/34376 "https://indianapolis.granicus.com/boards/w/f4a1ea9c05a8da69/boards/34376")

### Become a board member

To become a board member, you must be a resident of the Consolidated City. Voting members come from the six IMPD districts. Sworn law enforcement officers are not eligible to serve as voting members. [Click here to apply.](https://indianapolis.granicus.com/boards/w/f4a1ea9c05a8da69/boards/34376 "https://indianapolis.granicus.com/boards/w/f4a1ea9c05a8da69/boards/34376")

CPCO No. 20-007 

  • NAME: William Sluder
  • RANK: Patrol Officer
  • DATE COMPLAINT FILED: January 28, 2020
  • ALLEGED VIOLATION: IMPD General Order 4.25 - INCIDENT REPORTING - Policy: It is the policy of the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department (IMPD) to ensure uniformity, thoroughness, accuracy, and completeness in incident reporting. The incident report ensures uniformity in reporting procedures and is the official record concerning the investigation of an incident or offense. Incident reports are critical in determining statistics, personnel and equipment needs, and crime analysis. Therefore, the completed report must be precise and contain enough information to accurately reflect the reported incident. Whenever a citizen requests a report be made, it is the policy of this department that an officer will complete an incident report.
  • CPCB FINDING/DISPOSITION: Exonerated (The allegation made in the complaint is false or not factual, or the conduct complained of was lawful and proper.) 

CPCO No. 20-011 

  • NAME: Tracy Knecht
  • RANK: Patrol Officer
  • DATE COMPLAINT FILED: February 10, 2020
  • FIRST ALLEGED VIOLATION: IMPD Rules and Regulations Section II - ANY BREACH OF DISCIPLINE: (A) Members shall not conduct themselves in a manner which is detrimental to the efficient operation and/or general discipline of the department.
  • CPCB FINDING/DISPOSITION: Not Sustained (There is insufficient evidence to prove the allegation made in the complaint by clear and convincing evidence.)
  • SECOND ALLEGED VIOLATION: MPD Rules and Regulations Section VI - CONDUCT UNBECOMING AN OFFICER: (A) When dealing with the public, members shall not use language or gestures which are rude, demeaning or affronting.
  • CPCB FINDING/DISPOSITION: Not Sustained (There is insufficient evidence to prove the allegation made in the complaint by clear and convincing evidence.)***End of Repo
